shared_definitions_and_bridges.coupling_definition: Pi(mu,nu) consists of probability measures pi on the product measurable space E x E whose first projection marginal is mu and second projection marginal is nu.
shared_definitions_and_bridges.cost_definition: C_c(mu,nu) is the infimum, in the extended nonnegative reals [0,infinity], of the nonnegative integrals of c over pi in Pi(mu,nu). The integral uses the natural embedding of the finite nonnegative cost into [0,infinity].
shared_definitions_and_bridges.measurability_bridge: Measurable X_t and X_s give measurable omega -> (X_t(omega),X_s(omega)) into the product sigma algebra. The open-set measurability assumption on E x E makes every continuous real or nonnegative-real cost/test on that product measurable.
shared_definitions_and_bridges.compactness_bridge: E x E is compact. A finite continuous nonnegative cost is bounded above by some finite K depending only on c and E. Hence its integral under any probability coupling is at most K. The same argument gives a K^2 bound for c^2.
shared_definitions_and_bridges.coupling_existence_bridge: The joint pushforward of the same sample at t and s is an actual coupling, by composing pushforwards with the two projections. Thus every pair of the displayed marginals has a coupling; empty-infimum behavior is never used.
shared_definitions_and_bridges.empty_case_boundary: No explicit nonemptiness assumption is needed. Conclusions with no time points or no points in T x E are vacuous. Whenever a stated time exists, the probability law and given state-valued slice supply the nonempty state situation needed for actual evaluations.

source.title: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost
source.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). For every fixed \(s\in T\), the Kantorovich cost with cost \(c\) from \(\mu_t\) to \(\mu_s\) tends to zero as \(t\to s\). The limit is in the extended nonnegative reals.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
source.boundary: The cost need not be a metric or symmetric. Compactness and the finite continuous cost are retained. This is a limit at each fixed time, without a quantitative rate.

proof.title: Use the same sample at two times
proof.text: The paired process \(Z_t=(X_t,X_s)\) has continuous sample paths on the original full event. The marginal-law theorem therefore makes \(\gamma_t=(Z_t)_\#P\) weakly continuous. Its two marginals are \(\mu_t,\mu_s\).

proof.title: Integrate the continuous cost
proof.text: Compactness bounds the continuous cost, and the measurable-open-set assumption makes it measurable. Its integral is continuous in the probability law. At \(s\), both coordinates coincide, so this cost integral is zero.

proof.title: Bound the infimum by this coupling
proof.text: The transport cost is nonnegative and at most the cost of the explicit coupling. Squeezing gives the asserted limit.

source.title: A transport estimate gives joint continuity
source.statement: Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). Let \(F\) be a normed additive commutative group, \(U:T\times E\to F\) any field, and \(L\in\mathbb R\). Suppose the bound below holds for every pair \((t,x),(s,y)\). Then \(U\) is jointly continuous. Here \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) denotes the probability couplings. The map \(\operatorname{toReal}\) takes the ordinary real value at finite inputs and sends \(\infty\) to zero; the costs \(Q(t,s)\) here are finite by compactness and the explicit same-sample coupling.
assumptions: \(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.
\(F\) is a normed additive commutative group; no scalar action or completeness is required.
The displayed estimate holds for all pairs in \(T\times E\), with one real constant \(L\). No sign assumption on \(L\), or prior regularity of \(U\), is required.
source.boundary: The estimate is an explicit input to this general continuity principle. A model application must establish it separately. The proof uses continuity of the extended-real toReal map at zero; no separate finite-cost premise is inserted.

proof.title: Apply the transport limit to the squared cost
proof.text: Fix \(q=(s,y)\). The squared cost is continuous, nonnegative and zero on the diagonal. The preceding theorem, composed with the time projection, gives the transport limit.

proof.title: Make the majorant tend to zero
proof.text: The real-value map is continuous at the finite value zero, and square root is continuous. The point cost tends to its diagonal value. Adding these terms and multiplying by the fixed real constant gives a vanishing majorant.

proof.title: Squeeze the norm difference
proof.text: The assumed estimate bounds the nonnegative norm by that majorant. The norm difference tends to zero at every \(q\), which is joint continuity.

definitions.squared_cost: c^2(z)=c(z)^2, still a continuous finite nonnegative cost with diagonal value zero.
definitions.transport_quantity: Q(t,s)=C_{c^2}(mu_t,mu_s), an extended-nonnegative-real infimum over the same probability-coupling convention.
definitions.target_group: F is a normed additive commutative group. Subtraction and its norm are available; scalar multiplication or completeness of F is not required.
definitions.field: U:T x E -> F is an arbitrary function before the transport estimate is imposed.
definitions.estimate_constant: L is one fixed real number used for every ordered pair (t,x),(s,y); it need not be nonnegative.
definitions.toReal: The total map [0,infinity] -> R equals the ordinary real value at every finite input and maps infinity to zero. Under the stated compactness and finite-continuous-cost assumptions, every displayed Q(t,s) is finite, so the infinite-input convention is never needed for its value.
definitions.majorant_at_fixed_q: For q=(s,y), H_q(t,x)=L*(sqrt(toReal Q(t,s))+c(x,y)), interpreted as a real scalar with the finite cost coerced to R.

Then U is continuous at every q=(s,y), hence continuous on T x E.

The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.

scope.estimate_scope: One pointwise inequality for all pairs, with one global real L. The estimate is an explicit application obligation, not a consequence proved from path continuity.
scope.continuity_scope: Ordinary joint topological continuity at every product point. Neither E nor T x E is assumed first-countable; the proof uses continuous projection to the time limit from the first theorem.
scope.path_scope: The same one-event whole-T path continuity and all-slice measurability as in the first statement.
scope.target_scope: Only the normed additive group structure is used through norm subtraction, nonnegativity and the norm characterization of continuity.
scope.not_claimed: No estimate derivation for a specific model, no Lipschitz modulus in a metric on T x E, no differentiability, and no quantitative rate.

units.constant_dependencies: L precedes the universal all-pairs inequality and is independent of t,s,x,y. It may be chosen from the overall field/model data. Auxiliary compactness bounds for c^2 depend only on c and E; no finite-cost or sign premise is added.
